What you see: The loss climbs, bounces, or shows "nan"
A possible cause: The learning rate may be too high
What to try: Lower it by a factor of ten

A possible cause: The learning rate may be too low, or the walk is on a plateau
What to try: Raise the rate, or try momentum or Adam

What you see: Training stops at the step limit
What to try: Read the warning. Allow more steps or fix the scaling

A possible cause: Inputs may be on very different scales

What you see: The answer hovers and never settles
A possible cause: A constant learning rate with stochastic gradient descent
Random starting weights or batch order, with no fixed seed
What to try: Fix the seed and record it

A possible cause: Possibly local minimums, or training that stopped before it finished
What to try: Train longer, and from several starts, and keep the best

What you see: Training error keeps falling, new data gets worse
What to try: Check error on held-back data. Stop earlier, simplify the model, or get more data

A possible cause: The model may be the wrong shape, or the loss measures the wrong thing
What to try: Change the model or the loss. More training won't help
